react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct activity) converged on steroid hormone biosynthesis as the dominant affected pathway. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) at rank 0 with p=5.77e-07, driven by six input steroids. Mummichog ranked the empirical-compound analogue 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' at rank 0 (p=1.68e-04) with 14 matched compounds including all eight input metabolites. RaMP multi-DB ORA independently confirmed KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at FDR 4.97e-18 with six hits, alongside the Reactome super-pathway 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (R-HSA-196071, FDR 4.38e-17, six hits) and WikiPathways 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496, FDR 1.37e-16, five hits). The eight input metabolites span the C18/C19/C21 steroid scaffold — DHEA, androstenedione, testosterone, dihydrotestosterone, estrone, and estradiol occupy the androgen-to-estrogen interconversion axis, while 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde maps to tyrosine metabolism (mummichog rank 2, p=0.027), a branch linked to dopamine and norepinephrine biosynthesis. Warfarin, a CYP2C9 substrate and indirect modulator of steroid catabolism enzymes, was also detected but did not directly map to the steroid biosynthesis roster. Across the three paradigms, the cross-paradigm winner is the KEGG:hsa00140/SMPDB:SMP00068 steroid hormone axis, with six driver steroids confirmed in the metabolites_hit rosters of both the RaMP and MetaboAnalystR results.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant affected system. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' and KEGG:map00150 as top hits (FDR 4.97e-18, six overlapping steroids). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00140 first (p=5.77e-07, six steroids: DHEA, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, 17β-estradiol, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 0 (p=8.40e-05, 14 matched compounds including all six steroid inputs). The cross-paradigm winner is the androgen-and-estrogen axis captured by SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:hsa00140. The six steroid driver metabolites (17β-estradiol, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, DHEA, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one) were confirmed in the metabolites_hit rosters of both RaMP and MetaboAnalystR. A secondary hit, MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (p=0.028), was driven solely by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde. Warfarin (C01541) did not map to any steroid pathway but appears in the input set; its clinical relevance may involve CYP2C9-mediated drug-steroid interactions rather than direct pathway membership. The converging evidence identifies androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism as the primary perturbed pathway.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on steroid hormone metabolism as the dominant affected system. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned SMPDB:SMP00068 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' and KEGG:map00150 as top hits (FDR 4.97e-18, six overlapping steroids). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked KEGG:hsa00140 first (p=5.77e-07, six steroids: DHEA, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, 17β-estradiol, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one). Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism at rank 0 (p=8.40e-05, 14 matched compounds including all six steroid inputs). The cross-paradigm winner is the androgen-and-estrogen axis captured by SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:hsa00140. The six steroid driver metabolites (17β-estradiol, testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, DHEA, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one) were confirmed in the metabolites_hit rosters of both RaMP and MetaboAnalystR. A secondary hit, MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism (p=0.028), was driven solely by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde. Warfarin (C01541) did not map to any steroid pathway but appears in the input set; its clinical relevance may involve CYP2C9-mediated drug-steroid interactions rather than direct pathway membership. The converging evidence identifies androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism as the primary perturbed pathway.
